jee_king_q1.name: jee_king_q1
jee_king_q1.question: integrate sin(x)/(sin(x) + cos(x)) from 0 to pi/2
steps: Apply King's Property: I = ∫ [0 to 1.571] f(x) dx = ∫ [0 to 1.571] f(1.571 - x) dx
Add both integral forms: 2*I = ∫ [0 to 1.571] [f(x) + f(1.571 - x)] dx
Algebraic Simplification: f(x) + f(1.571 - x) = 1 (Identically Constant)
jee_king_q1.notes: Classic King property problem | Remember to multiply by 1/2 after adding flipped integral!

gaussian_proof.name: gaussian_proof
gaussian_proof.question: web solve exp(-x^2)
steps: Recognized Liouville-proven non-elementary integrand f(x) = exp(-x^2).
By Liouville's Theorem on differential fields, no elementary closed-form antiderivative exists.
The exact analytic antiderivative is defined via the Gauss Error Function: erf(x) = (2 / sqrt(pi)) * ∫[0 to x] exp(-t^2) dt.
Maclaurin series expansion: ∫ ∑[n=0..∞] ((-1)^n x^(2n) / n!) dx = ∑[n=0..∞] ((-1)^n x^(2n+1) / (n! * (2n+1))) + C.
